examples.ko: 이 기계는 전원을 켜면 바로 작동돼요.
examples.en: This machine runs as soon as you turn the power on.
The elevator hasn't worked since yesterday.
I'll check whether the app worked properly.
When the emergency bell goes off, it makes a loud sound.
Not a single computer works.

examples.ko: 이 시계는 배터리 없이도 작동될 거예요.
examples.en: This watch will run even without a battery.

explain: 기계나 프로그램이 움직이는 모습을 말할 때 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '작동하다'도 써요. 안 될 때는 '작동이 안 돼요'라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it for machines or programs that are running. '작동하다' works the same way. When something fails, you say '작동이 안 돼요'.

examples.en: Click the blue button.
I clicked the link by mistake.
If you click the photo twice, it gets bigger.

examples.ko: 여기를 클릭하라고 했는데 아무 일도 안 일어나요.
examples.en: They said to click here, but nothing happens.
It makes a sound every time I click.
The menu I clicked disappeared.

explain: 컴퓨터에서 쓰는 외래어 동사예요. 휴대폰 화면에서는 '누르다'나 '터치하다'도 써요. '클릭'은 명사로도 써서 '클릭 한 번'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: A loanword verb used on computers. On a phone screen you can also say '누르다' or '터치하다'. The noun '클릭' works too, as in '클릭 한 번'.

en: be expanded; be enlarged; be increased

examples.en: When you tap the photo, the screen zooms in.
The scale of the business grew a lot this year.
It is easy to read because the letters are enlarged.
Support will be extended to young people too.
The child laughed at the picture getting bigger.
I'll tell you before the problem gets bigger.

explain: 크기나 범위가 커질 때 써요. 반대말은 '축소되다'예요. 사람이 크게 만들면 '확대하다'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it when size or range grows. The opposite is '축소되다'. When a person enlarges something, use '확대하다'.

examples.ko: 회의 날짜를 이번 주 금요일로 확정해요.
examples.en: We are fixing the meeting date for this Friday.
The team leader finalized the plan.
Let me know when you finalize the schedule.
Nothing has been decided yet.
We will finalize the result next week.
I'll post the ad after we fix the price.

explain: 아직 바뀔 수 있던 것을 마지막으로 정할 때 써요. '정하다'보다 격식 있어서 일정, 가격, 결과 이야기에 어울려요. 정해진 상태는 '확정되다'예요.
explain_en: Use it when you settle something that could still change. It is more formal than '정하다' and fits schedules, prices, and results. The settled state is '확정되다'.

examples.en: This company supplies vegetables to restaurants.
The government supplied masks for free.
The pipe that supplies water burst.
I'm sorry we couldn't supply enough goods.
We will supply electricity to the factory.
We get paid right away when we supply the parts.

explain: 물건, 전기, 물을 계속 대 줄 때 써요. 받는 쪽에서는 '공급받다'라고 해요. 시장에서는 '수요'(필요로 하는 양)와 짝으로 나와요.
explain_en: Use it for continuously providing goods, electricity, or water. From the receiving side you say '공급받다'. In economics it pairs with '수요' (the amount people need).

en: be deleted; be removed; be eliminated

examples.en: The file got deleted because I pressed it by mistake.
Old messages are deleted automatically.
I hope my post isn't deleted.
Save the photos before they are deleted.

examples.ko: 삭제된 파일은 휴지통에서 찾을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can find deleted files in the trash.
This comment will be deleted soon.

explain: 컴퓨터나 인터넷의 글, 파일이 지워질 때 써요. 지우는 사람이 주어이면 '삭제하다'예요. 연필로 쓴 글씨는 보통 '지우다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it when files or posts on a computer or the internet are removed. If a person is the subject, use '삭제하다'. For pencil writing, people usually say '지우다'.

examples.en: A famous director directs this drama.
He directed the play himself.
I want to create a warm atmosphere.
The film I directed won an award.

examples.ko: 조명으로 밤 분위기를 연출할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can create a night mood with lighting.

examples.ko: 연출하는 사람은 배우들과 이야기를 많이 해요.
examples.en: The person who directs talks a lot with the actors.

explain: 영화나 연극에서 '연출'은 감독이 하는 일이에요. 그래서 '연출자'라는 말도 있어요. 분위기나 장면을 일부러 만든다는 뜻으로 일상에서도 써요.
explain_en: In films and plays, '연출' is the director's job, which is why '연출자' exists. In everyday talk it also means deliberately setting up a mood or scene.

examples.en: He carves faces out of stone.
My grandfather carved a bird out of wood.
I watched the carving up close.
They carved ice to make a decoration.
The carved work is in the museum.
If you carve soap, it becomes a pretty flower.

explain: '조각'은 케이크 한 조각의 '조각'과 소리가 같지만 다른 말이에요. 예술의 '조각'은 '조각가'가 나무나 돌을 깎는 일이에요. 글자나 무늬를 파서 남기는 일은 '새기다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '조각' also means a piece, as in a piece of cake, but that is a different word with the same sound. The art word '조각' is what a '조각가' (sculptor) does with wood or stone. '새기다' is a related word for engraving.

examples.en: The boss gives instructions to the staff.
The teacher told us to do the homework first.
The doctor instructed me to take the medicine.
Is it okay if I do it as you instructed?
The team leader speaks clearly when giving instructions.
Don't do anything I haven't instructed.

explain: 회사나 학교에서 윗사람이 아랫사람에게 할 일을 정해 줄 때 써요. 친구에게 부탁할 때는 쓰지 않아요. '시키다'는 일상에서 더 가볍게 써요.
explain_en: Used when a superior assigns work to someone below at a company or school. You do not use it when asking a friend. '시키다' is a lighter everyday alternative.

examples.en: My health improved after I took the medicine.
The service is getting better little by little.
If the environment improves, more people gather.
I can see the parts that are improving.
This problem needs to be improved quickly.
I hope the mood in the room gets much better.

explain: 나쁜 부분이 좋아질 때 써요. 상태, 제도, 서비스처럼 고칠 수 있는 것에 어울려요. 날씨나 기분이 좋아질 때는 '좋아지다'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it when a weak part gets better. It fits things you can fix, such as conditions, systems, or services. For weather or mood, say '좋아지다'.

examples.en: The same mistake keeps repeating.
It feels like the days repeat exactly the same.
If the work repeats, it gets boring.
I'll be careful so the same thing doesn't happen again.
Today repeated the same thing as yesterday.
Thanks to repeated practice, I became good at it.

explain: 같은 일이 다시 일어날 때 써요. 내가 하면 '반복하다', 저절로 되풀이되면 '반복되다'예요. 순우리말로는 '되풀이되다'가 있어요.
explain_en: Use it when the same thing happens again. If you do it, it is '반복하다'; if it just recurs, '반복되다'. A native Korean equivalent is '되풀이되다'.

examples.en: There was a fire, so everyone escaped from the building.
The hero in the movie escapes from prison.
To escape, you have to go out through this door.
No one has escaped from there.
Let's look for a way to escape together.
I tried a game where you escape from a room.

explain: 갇힌 곳이나 위험한 곳에서 빠져나올 때 써요. '도망치다'는 쫓기는 느낌이 있고, '탈출하다'는 어렵게 벗어나는 느낌이 있어요. 조사는 '~에서 탈출하다'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it for getting out of a trapped or dangerous place. '도망치다' feels like running from a chaser, while '탈출하다' feels like breaking free with difficulty. The pattern is '~에서 탈출하다'.

examples.en: I'm replacing the light bulb with a new one.
I replaced the old tires.

examples.ko: 선수를 교체하면 경기가 달라질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you substitute a player, the game can change.
The part to be replaced hasn't arrived yet.

examples.ko: 배터리를 교체하는 데 오 분 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes five minutes to replace the battery.
The sound has been good since I replaced it.

explain: 낡은 것을 새것으로 바꿀 때 써요. 서로 맞바꾸는 '교환하다'와 달라요. 사람에게도 써서 선수나 담당자를 '교체하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it when you swap an old thing for a new one. It differs from '교환하다', which is trading one for another. It also applies to people, such as players or the person in charge.

examples.en: The police detained the criminal.
I feel like the promise is binding me.
He tries to control his partner and calls it love.
The court decides whether to detain that person.
If you restrict a child too much, the child feels stifled.
I hope rules don't tie people down.

explain: 뉴스에서는 경찰이나 법원이 사람을 잡아 가둘 때 써요. 일상에서는 자유롭게 못 하게 묶는다는 뜻으로 써요. 명사 '구속'도 두 경우에 모두 써요.
explain_en: In the news it means police or courts detaining someone. In daily life it means tying someone down so they lack freedom. The noun '구속' covers both.

examples.en: Our company trades with many countries.
Korea has traded with China for a long time.
People who trade check the exchange rate often.
To trade with other countries, you need many documents.
Price matters when you trade rice.
I decided which goods I want to trade.

explain: 나라 사이에 물건을 사고팔 때 써요. 보통 '무역을 하다'로 말해요. 내보내는 것은 '수출', 들여오는 것은 '수입'이에요.
explain_en: Use it for buying and selling goods between countries. People usually say '무역을 하다'. Sending goods out is '수출', bringing them in is '수입'.

examples.en: I trust our team leader.
Customers don't trust this shop.

examples.ko: 친구를 신뢰하면 비밀도 말할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you trust a friend, you can share secrets too.

examples.ko: 신뢰할 수 있는 정보만 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please give me only information I can trust.
This is the doctor I trust.
I trusted him, but he lied.

explain: '믿다'보다 격식 있는 말이에요. 회사, 정보, 사람처럼 쌓아 온 믿음에 어울려요. 명사 '신뢰'는 '신뢰를 얻다', '신뢰를 잃다'로 써요.
explain_en: It is more formal than '믿다'. It fits trust built up in a company, a source, or a person. The noun is used as '신뢰를 얻다' and '신뢰를 잃다'.

examples.en: Old paintings are on display at the museum.
My work was displayed in the lobby.

examples.ko: 전시되는 옷은 만져 볼 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't touch the clothes on display.
The photos will be on display until next month.
The ring displayed in the glass case is pretty.
Do you want to go see the paintings when they are displayed?

explain: 보여 주려고 놓인 물건이 주어일 때 써요. 사람이나 기관이 보여 주면 '전시하다'예요. 가게나 박물관 이야기에 나와요.
explain_en: Use it when the object put out for viewing is the subject. If a person or institution shows it, use '전시하다'. It appears in talk about shops and museums.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 새 옷을 창문 쪽에 전시해요.
examples.en: This shop displays new clothes by the window.
We displayed the pictures the students made in the hallway.
To exhibit your work, you have to apply.
I'm choosing the photos to exhibit.
Where do you want to display it?
The paintings shown at the gallery are great.

explain: 사람이나 기관이 주어일 때 써요. 물건이 주어이면 '전시되다'예요. 보러 가는 행사는 '전시회'라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it when a person or institution is the subject. If the object is the subject, use '전시되다'. The event you visit is called '전시회'.

examples.en: A new problem was raised.
Various opinions are raised in the meeting.
I'll answer the questions being raised one by one.
When a problem is raised, we check right away.
Let's solve the problems already raised first.
I explained every time a doubt was raised.

explain: 문제, 의혹, 질문 같은 말이 나올 때만 써요. 앞에 보통 '문제가', '의견이'가 와요. 사람이 꺼내면 '제기하다'예요.
explain_en: Use it only when issues, doubts, or questions come up. It is usually preceded by '문제가' or '의견이'. When a person raises it, use '제기하다'.

examples.en: A new singer is born today.
Do you know how this song came to be?
I took a photo of the moment it was born.
When a new government is born, policies change.
She is the first writer to come out of our class.
I think a good film will be born.

explain: '태어나다'는 사람과 동물에게 일상에서 써요. '탄생하다'는 새 나라, 작품, 스타처럼 큰 의미가 있을 때 써요. 대화에서 사람이 태어난 이야기는 '태어나다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '태어나다' is the everyday word for people and animals. '탄생하다' fits significant beginnings like a new country, a work, or a star. For a person's birth in conversation, '태어나다' sounds natural.

examples.en: That song moved everyone.
I want to move my parents with a letter.
It is a film that moves people.
A small gift touches a friend.
What touched the teacher was the student's effort.

examples.ko: 말만으로는 그 사람을 감동시킬 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't move that person with words alone.

explain: 느끼게 하는 쪽이 주어예요. 느끼는 사람이 주어이면 '감동받다'를 써요. '노래가 나를 감동시켰어요'와 '나는 노래에 감동받았어요'를 비교해 보세요.
explain_en: The subject is whoever causes the feeling. If the person who feels it is the subject, use '감동받다'. Compare '노래가 나를 감동시켰어요' with '나는 노래에 감동받았어요'.

en: act on behalf of; handle for someone

examples.en: The travel agency handles the visa application for you.
The manager acted in place of the boss.
How much is the fee at a company that handles moving for you?

examples.ko: 청소를 대행해 주는 서비스를 써 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried a service that does the cleaning for you.
To act on someone's behalf here, you need permission.

examples.ko: 제가 대행할 수 있는 일은 많지 않아요.
examples.en: There aren't many things I can do on someone's behalf.

explain: 다른 사람이나 회사의 일을 대신 해 줄 때 써요. 서비스 이름에 많아서 '대행사', '대행 수수료'라는 말이 있어요. 친구 일은 보통 '대신 해 주다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it when you do someone else's work for them, especially as a service. That is why words like '대행사' and '대행 수수료' exist. For a friend's task, people usually say '대신 해 주다'.

examples.en: Citizens were outraged by the unfair decision.
People get furious when they hear the news.
It's hard to calm an angry heart.
The furious customer shouted.
If you get too angry, your words become rough.
It's nothing to be furious about, so why are you like this?

explain: '화나다'보다 크고 무거운 감정이에요. 사회 문제나 불공평한 일에 많이 써요. 가벼운 일에는 '화나다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: A bigger, heavier feeling than '화나다'. It is often used for social issues or unfair events. For small matters, '화나다' sounds natural.

examples.en: There is a presidential election next year.

examples.ko: 대선 날에는 투표소가 일찍 문을 열어요.
examples.en: On election day, the polling stations open early.
The presidential candidates debated on TV.
Voter turnout was high in the last presidential election.
The presidential election result comes out tonight.
I'm voting for the first time in this presidential election.

explain: 대통령 선거를 줄인 말이에요. 국회의원 선거는 '총선'이라고 해요. '대선 후보', '대선 투표'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여 써요.
explain_en: It is short for the presidential election. A parliamentary election is called '총선'. It attaches before other words, as in '대선 후보' and '대선 투표'.

examples.en: Artists create new worlds.
He created a style of his own.
The goal is to create new jobs.

examples.ko: 창조하려면 먼저 많이 보고 들어야 해요.
examples.en: To create, you first have to see and hear a lot.

examples.ko: 이 게임은 사용자가 직접 캐릭터를 창조할 수 있어요.
examples.en: In this game, users can create characters themselves.
I showed my friends the story I created.

explain: 아무것도 없던 곳에서 새것을 만들어 낼 때 써요. '만들다'는 일상 말이고 '창조하다'는 예술, 종교, 큰 일에 써요. 글이나 음악 같은 작품은 '창작하다'도 써요.
explain_en: Use it for bringing something new out of nothing. '만들다' is the everyday word; '창조하다' fits art, religion, and big endeavors. For works like writing or music, '창작하다' is also used.

examples.en: I test the new program first.
I tested the app yesterday and it went well.
I'll tell you about the problems after testing.

examples.ko: 테스트할 때는 여러 번 해 봐야 해요.
examples.en: When you test, you have to try several times.
Please wait a moment while we test.

examples.ko: 신제품을 직접 테스트한 사람이 후기를 썼어요.
examples.en: A person who tested the new product wrote a review.

explain: 제품, 프로그램, 기능이 되는지 확인해 볼 때 써요. 학교 시험은 '시험'이라고 해요. '시험하다'도 있지만 일상 대화에서는 외래어 '테스트'를 자주 들어요.
explain_en: Use it when checking whether a product, program, or feature works. A school exam is called '시험'. '시험하다' also exists, but in daily talk you will hear the loanword '테스트'.

examples.en: Earth is a planet that goes around the sun.
Jupiter is the biggest planet.

examples.ko: 다른 행성에도 사람이 살 수 있을까요?
examples.en: Could people live on other planets too?

examples.ko: 이 망원경으로 행성을 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see planets with this telescope.
I memorized the names of the planets in order.

examples.ko: 영화 속 외계인은 작은 행성에서 왔어요.
examples.en: The alien in the movie came from a small planet.

explain: '별'과 구분해요. 태양처럼 스스로 빛나는 것은 '항성'이고, 지구, 화성, 목성은 '행성'이에요. 일상에서는 별을 모두 '별'이라고 부르기도 해요.
explain_en: Do not confuse it with '별'. A self-lit star like the sun is a '항성'; Earth, Mars, and Jupiter are '행성'. In daily speech people often call all of them '별'.

examples.en: City Hall approved the construction.
My parents allowed me to go out.
You can't enter unless it's permitted.
This park permits taking photos.

examples.ko: 관리자가 허가한 사람만 문을 열 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only the people the manager has permitted can open the door.
I'll let you know tomorrow whether we'll permit it.

explain: 관청이나 윗사람이 해도 된다고 공식적으로 말할 때 써요. '허락'은 개인 사이에서 더 자연스러워요. 친구에게는 '해도 돼'라고 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when an authority or superior officially says yes. '허락' sounds more natural between individuals. With a friend you would simply say '해도 돼'.

examples.en: The professor lectures every Monday.
She taught Korean at a university.
The way he lectures is fun.
To teach online, you need a camera.
The topic I will lecture on is Hangul.
I took questions after lecturing.

explain: 대학이나 학원에서 길게 가르칠 때 써요. 학교 수업은 보통 '수업'이라고 하고 가르치는 일은 '가르치다'라고 해요. 듣는 사람은 '강의를 듣다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: Used for teaching at length at a university or academy. School classes are usually '수업', and teaching in general is '가르치다'. The listener says '강의를 듣다'.

examples.en: I didn't mean to say that.
Let's think about what the author intended.
I didn't do it on purpose.
It didn't go the way I intended.

examples.ko: 광고를 만든 사람은 사람들이 웃도록 의도했어요.
examples.en: The person who made the ad intended people to laugh.

examples.ko: 그 일을 처음부터 의도했다면 더 큰 문제가 돼요.
examples.en: If you intended that from the start, it becomes a bigger problem.

explain: '의도'는 마음속의 목적이에요. 사과할 때 '의도하지 않았어요'라고 말할 수 있어요. '일부러'는 더 일상적인 말이에요.
explain_en: '의도' is the purpose in your mind. When apologizing you can say '의도하지 않았어요'. '일부러' is the more casual everyday word.

examples.ko: 오늘 밤 열두 시에 행사가 종료돼요.
examples.en: The event ends at midnight tonight.
The program suddenly shut down.
When the contract ends, you have to apply again.
Check the date it ends.
It's a service that will end soon.
It's an event that has already ended.

explain: 행사, 계약, 서비스처럼 끝나는 때가 있는 것이 끝날 때 써요. '끝나다'보다 격식 있어요. 컴퓨터 화면에서도 '종료'를 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: Use it when something with a set end, like an event, contract, or service, comes to an end. It is more formal than '끝나다'. You also see '종료' on computer screens.

examples.ko: 저는 다 쓰고 나면 앱을 바로 종료해요.
examples.en: When I'm done, I close the app right away.
We ended the meeting early.
Press this button to close the program.
Be sure to save before you quit the game.
It's time to end the class.
Close it and then turn it back on.

explain: 끝내는 사람이 있으면 '종료하다', 저절로 끝나면 '종료되다'예요. 컴퓨터나 앱을 끌 때도 써요. 일상에서는 '끝내다'를 더 편하게 써요.
explain_en: If someone ends it, use '종료하다'; if it ends on its own, '종료되다'. You also use it to close a computer or app. In daily talk, '끝내다' is the easier word.

examples.en: I secure the ladder to the wall.
I fastened the desk leg with nails.
If you don't fix it in place, it wobbles.
I fixed the camera in place and shot it.
I'll pin this post to the top.
When the price is fixed, customers feel reassured.

explain: 움직이지 않게 붙이거나 묶을 때 써요. 값이나 위치를 바꾸지 않을 때도 써요. 저절로 그런 상태가 되면 '고정되다'예요.
explain_en: Use it for fastening something so it doesn't move. It also covers keeping a price or position unchanged. When it just ends up that way, use '고정되다'.

en: be in the way; be a hindrance; get in the way

examples.en: Loud noise gets in the way of studying.
I'm sorry if I was in the way.
I'll go in quietly so I won't disturb anyone.
Please move the things that are in the way.

examples.ko: 이어폰 소리가 옆 사람에게 방해될까 봐 줄였어요.
examples.en: I turned down my earphones in case they bothered the person next to me.
Tell me if it bothers you.

explain: 어떤 일에 걸림돌이 될 때 써요. '방해가 되다'라고도 해요. 정중하게 '방해되지 않을까요?'라고 물을 수 있어요.
explain_en: Use it when something gets in the way of an activity. You can also say '방해가 되다'. A polite way to ask is '방해되지 않을까요?'.

examples.en: The dove symbolizes peace.
The color red symbolized luck in this country.
This building is a place that represents the city.
They say a ring symbolizes a promise.
This painting symbolizes family.

examples.ko: 마음을 상징할 수 있는 모양을 골랐어요.
examples.en: I chose a shape that can symbolize a feeling.

explain: 비둘기=평화처럼 눈에 보이는 것이 보이지 않는 뜻을 대신할 때 써요. '~은/는 ~을 상징해요' 형태로 말해요. 명사 '상징'은 '평화의 상징'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it when something visible stands for an unseen idea, like a dove for peace. The pattern is '~은/는 ~을 상징해요'. The noun is used as '평화의 상징'.

examples.en: The store is cutting its prices.
The bank lowered the interest rate.
If you lower the price, customers increase.
They are looking for ways to cut taxes.
They plan to lower the fee.
We are selling at the reduced price.

explain: 가격, 이자, 세금 같은 숫자를 내릴 때 써요. 반대말은 '인상하다'예요. '값을 내리다'보다 격식 있는 말이에요.
explain_en: Use it when lowering numbers like prices, interest, or taxes. The opposite is '인상하다'. It is more formal than '값을 내리다'.

examples.en: My older sister got pregnant not long ago.
When you're pregnant, you have to be careful about what you eat.
I gave my seat to a pregnant friend.
I'm on leave from work because I'm pregnant.
I got checked at the hospital before getting pregnant.
We are getting ready to have a baby.

explain: 지금 임신 중인 상태는 과거형 '임신했어요'로 말해요. 가까운 사이에서는 '아기가 생겼어요'라고도 해요. 병원이나 뉴스에서는 '임신'을 써요.
explain_en: The current state of being pregnant is expressed in the past form '임신했어요'. Among close people you can also say '아기가 생겼어요'. Hospitals and the news use '임신'.

examples.en: I regret not saying it back then.
I bought expensive shoes and regretted it right away.
Do your best so you won't regret it.
There is nothing I regret.
I bought it because I thought I'd regret it later.
If you regret it, you can just start again.

explain: '후회하다'는 내가 의식적으로 후회할 때, '후회되다'는 마음이 저절로 그렇게 될 때 써요. '~ㄴ 게 후회돼요' 형태로 자주 말해요. 명사 '후회'는 '후회가 돼요'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '후회하다' is the act of regretting; '후회되다' is when the feeling arises by itself. A common form is '~ㄴ 게 후회돼요'. With the noun you can say '후회가 돼요'.

examples.en: I switch my phone to airplane mode.

examples.ko: 무음 모드라서 전화 소리가 안 났어요.
examples.en: The phone didn't ring because it was on silent mode.
If you change the screen mode, it is easier on the eyes.

examples.ko: 공부 모드에 들어가면 휴대폰을 안 봐요.
examples.en: When I go into study mode, I don't look at my phone.
This game has two modes.
Dark mode is good to use at night.

explain: 영어 mode에서 온 말이에요. 휴대폰이나 게임에서 '비행기 모드', '무음 모드'처럼 설정 상태를 말해요. '공부 모드'처럼 사람의 상태를 가볍게 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It comes from English 'mode'. On phones and games it names a setting, as in '비행기 모드' or '무음 모드'. People also say '공부 모드' lightly for their own state.

examples.en: Books are sorted by subject.
These clothes were classified as winter clothes.
Please tell me the criteria for sorting.
There are many unsorted documents.
If trash is sorted by type, recycling is easy.
I put the sorted photos in a folder.

explain: 나뉘어서 어느 칸에 들어갈 때 써요. 조사 '으로/로'와 같이 '~로 분류되다'라고 말해요. 나누는 사람이 주어이면 '분류하다'예요.
explain_en: Use it when something is divided and placed into a category. It goes with '으로/로', as in '~로 분류되다'. If a person does the sorting, use '분류하다'.

examples.en: Salary is paid on the 25th of every month.
The prize money was paid yesterday.
There is money that hasn't been paid yet.

examples.ko: 지급되는 물건은 마음대로 바꿀 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't change the items that are provided as you like.
You get a text when the money is paid.
It is scheduled to be paid soon.

explain: 돈이나 물건이 주어질 때 써요. 회사나 정부가 주면 '지급하다', 받는 쪽에서 말하면 '지급되다'예요. '월급', '지원금' 같은 말과 같이 나와요.
explain_en: Use it when money or goods are handed out. The giver (a company or government) uses '지급하다'; from the receiving side it is '지급되다'. It appears with words like '월급' and '지원금'.

examples.en: Customers decrease in winter.
Accidents decreased a lot compared to last year.
If trash decreases, it is good for the environment.
The rate of decrease is fast.
The cost that doesn't go down is the problem.
The population will keep decreasing.

explain: '감소하다'와 뜻이 같고, 보통은 '감소하다'를 더 많이 써요. 반대말은 '증가'예요. 사람 수, 비용, 사고처럼 숫자로 잴 수 있는 것이 줄 때 써요.
explain_en: It means the same as '감소하다', and '감소하다' is the more common form. The opposite is '증가'. Use it when things you can measure in numbers, like people, costs, or accidents, go down.

examples.en: The teacher stresses this part.
He emphasized the importance of practice.
If you emphasize it with color, it stands out.
I underlined the words I wanted to emphasize.
There are three points to emphasize.
What the boss stressed was safety.

explain: 더 중요하다고 힘주어 말할 때 써요. 글자를 굵게 하거나 줄을 치는 것도 '강조'예요. '강조점', '강조 표시'처럼 명사로도 써요.
explain_en: Use it when you stress that something is more important. Making text bold or underlining it is also '강조'. As a noun it appears in '강조점' and '강조 표시'.

examples.en: The two companies combine into one.
Water and oil don't combine.

examples.ko: 두 재료를 결합하면 새로운 맛이 나요.
examples.en: Combining the two ingredients gives a new flavor.

examples.ko: 한글은 자음과 모음을 결합해서 글자를 만들어요.
examples.en: Hangul builds letters by combining consonants and vowels.
The combined shape is interesting.

examples.ko: 서로 다른 생각을 결합할 수 있을까요?
examples.en: Can we combine different ideas?

explain: 서로 다른 둘이 합쳐져 하나가 될 때 써요. '합치다'보다 딱딱해서 과학, 기술, 문법 설명에 나와요. 'A와 B를 결합하다'나 'A가 B와 결합하다'로 써요.
explain_en: Use it when two different things join into one. It is stiffer than '합치다' and appears in science, technology, and grammar explanations. The patterns are 'A와 B를 결합하다' and 'A가 B와 결합하다'.
